brief: JPM retains its Tactically Bullish call after reassessing last week's AI-led selloff (SPX -2.0%, NDX -5.5%), concluding the Momentum/Tech Unwind and AI Credit Fears risks drove the drop while earnings (ASML, TSMC) and consumer data stayed resilient, so it reads the pullback as rotation, not a fundamental break. It favors cyclical exposure outside tech, selective buying of tech weakness (semis/memory) and banks after the earnings-driven pullback, prefers SPW over RTY to express broadening, and favors D1 baskets over sector ETFs as hedges as the Dispersion Index rises (30 to 37). On credit, hyperscaler spreads widened 12bp to 148bp (widest since July 2026) and JULI dispersion hit 21.2bp, but ratings have not deteriorated, so the strategist calls the widening overdone unless earnings show weakness; the trading desk frames the real stress as sitting with levered borrowers (neoclouds, data-center project finance, GPU deals), not hyperscalers. Rates strategist Jay Barry attributes last week's Treasury rally to AI valuation concerns, cleaner positioning and expected issuance cuts, and recommends 10s/30s steepeners. The positioning desk notes HF drawdown accelerated to -2.1% MTD but a +6% YTD cushion still favors a 4Q rally absent fundamental deterioration.
